# SEPSIS WITH SUSPECTED PNEUMONIA

Consider consulting Infectious Diseases if pneumonia is not strongly suspected as the source of infection.
Empirical regimens listed below have broad coverage of likely pathogens based on infectious site. Resistant gram-negative rods is not necessary in most patients except those with recent isolates of these organisms. Strongly consider rapid de-escalation of therapy in the first 24-48 hours based on MRSA nares, isolated pathogen(s), and patient response to therapy. Refer to pathogen specific sections of the Antimicrobial CDSS for additional treatment recommendations.

## Consider selecting alternative agents from separate drug class if recently treated with any of the above antibiotics.

---

References:

- Evans et al., Crit Care Med, 2021, 49(11):e1063-e1143.
- Mandell Chapter: Sepsis, Severe Sepsis and Septic Shock
- Rhee et al., Clinical Infectious Diseases, 2021, 72(4):541-552. PMID: 32374861
- Rhodes et al., Crit Care Med, 2022, 50(4):e413-e414. PMID: 34643578
- Sanford keyword: Sepsis, Adult
- Singer et al., JAMA, 2016, 315(8):801-810
- Up-to-date article: Sepsis syndromes in adults: Epidemiology, definitions, clinical presentation, diagnosis, and prognosis
Therapy:
## Inpatient

### Hospital acquired pneumonia preferred treatment

Recommend discontinuing vancomycin if MRSA nares return negative.
Piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q8H extended infustion <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12H
For penicillin allergy
<Substitute> Cefepime 2 gm IV q8h for Beta-lactam in regimen above

### Community acquired pneumonia preferred treatment

Ceftriaxone 2gm IV q24H <AND> azithromycin 500 mg PO once then 250mg PO q24H for 4 days
Recent Pseudomonas isolate:
Piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 gm IV q8H extended infusion <AND> azithromycin 500 mg PO once then 250 mg PO q24H for 4 days

### Severe beta-lactam reaction

[Treatment of Sepsis with Severe Beta-Lactam Reaction](sepsis-severe-beta-lactam-reaction)

### Recent MRSA isolate

<ADD> Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h to one of the above regimens

### Clinically unstable (ICU level care/hypotensive/tachycardic) AND recent multi-drug resistant gram-negative rod isolate

<ADD> Tobramycin 5 mg/kg IV x 1 dose to one of the above regimens *If CrCl less than 50 ml/min: 2 mg/kg x 1 dose (use order above and modify dose)
Pharmacy to follow

## ER/UC

### Nosocomial pneumonia preferred treatment

Recommend discontinuing vancomycin if MRSA nares return negative.
Piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 gm IV once STAT <AND> vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV once STAT
For penicillin allergy
<Substitute> Cefepime 2 gm once STAT for Beta-lactam in regimen above

### Community acquired pneumonia preferred treatment

Ceftriaxone 2gm IV once STAT <AND> azithromycin 500 mg PO once then 250 mg PO q24H for 4 days
Recent Pseudomonas isolate:
Piperacillin/tazobactam 4.5 gm IV once STAT <AND> azithromycin 500 mg PO once then 250 mg PO q24H for 4 days

### Severe beta-lactam reaction

[Treatment of Sepsis with Severe Beta-Lactam Reaction](sepsis-severe-beta-lactam-reaction)

### Recent MRSA isolate

<ADD> Vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV once STAT to one of the above regimens

### Clinically unstable (ICU level care/hypotensive/tachycardic) AND recent multi-drug resistant gram-negative rod isolate

<ADD> Tobramycin 5 mg/kg IV once STAT to one of the above regimens
*If CrCl < 50 ml/min: 2 mg/kg once STAT (use order above and modify dose)
Pharmacy to follow
